# casdoor_cert (Resource)

Manages a Casdoor cert, the key pair that signs tokens. Casdoor generates the certificate and private key when they are not set.

Only the attributes set in the configuration are written to Casdoor. The other fields of the object, including the ones not listed here, keep their current values.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The certificate and private key are generated by Casdoor.
resource "casdoor_cert" "acme" {
  name             = "cert-acme"
  display_name     = "Acme cert"
  scope            = "JWT"
  type             = "x509"
  crypto_algorithm = "RS256"
  bit_size         = 4096
  expire_in_years  = 20
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the cert, unique within its owner.

### Optional

- `bit_size` (Number) The key size in bits, e.g. `4096` for RS256.
- `certificate` (String) The PEM-encoded certificate.
- `crypto_algorithm` (String) The algorithm, e.g. `RS256`, `RS512`, `ES256`, `ES512` or `PS256`.
- `display_name` (String) The display name.
- `expire_in_years` (Number) The validity of the certificate, in years.
- `owner` (String) The owner of the object: `admin` for a global object shared by all organizations, or the name of an organization.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The PEM-encoded private key.
- `scope` (String) The scope, `JWT` or `CA`.
- `type` (String) The type, e.g. `x509`.

### Read-Only

- `created_time` (String) The time when the cert was created.
- `id` (String) The ID of the cert in the `owner/name` format.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the owner (admin or an organization) and the name.
terraform import casdoor_cert.example admin/<name>
```
